title: Sequenced slot adapter for variable-turn prompt/response workloads
creator: Ethan Rivera
description: Problem: In mixed prompt/response traffic (short prompts followed by long generations and vice versa) our continuous batching scheduler misallocates slot residency and KV cache capacity. This causes higher p95 latency for long responses during bursts and unnecessary KV thrashing for short-turn-heavy streams. Goal: implement a sequenced slot adapter that (1) classifies turn profiles at arrival, (2) reserves transient KV residency based on predicted continuation length, and (3) applies adaptive slot decay to free GPU slab space for high-variance workloads without increasing tail latency. Success metrics include p95 generation latency, tokens-per-second throughput, reduction in KV eviction rate, and net GPU memory uplift for mixed workloads.
acceptance_criteria: New scheduler reduces p95 generation latency for long-response-heavy traces by >=15% compared to baseline.
KV eviction rate decreases by >=25% on mixed turn workloads.
End-to-end token cost (GPU-seconds per 1M tokens) improves or stays flat for all observed traffic patterns.
Fallback mode exists that preserves current latency SLOs if model variant/slot adapter fails.
Bench dashboards added to Console with per-route delta visualizations and rollout controls.
proposal: Introduce a lightweight predictor at ingress that tags requests with a turn_profile: {single-short, short-then-long, long-then-short, multi-turn-long} using recent-session stats and quick length heuristic.

Sequenced slot adapter: a scheduling layer that allocates slots with one of three residency classes: transient (<8 tokens prefix), buffered (8-256 token warm reserve), and pinned (>256 tokens reserved). Allocation driven by turn_profile and current slab utilization.
KV residency smoothing: rather than immediate eviction when slab high-water reached, apply exponential decay windows by class (transient=10s, buffered=60s, pinned=300s) to absorb burstiness.
Adaptive slot decay: the scheduler computes decay_rate per-GPU that increases when fragmentation metric exceeds threshold and when average generation length variance > sigma_threshold.
Spill-to-host fallback: if slab pressure persists, coldest KV pages are migrated to pinned host memory pages (CPU RAM) with prefetch heuristics for next-token probability > 0.6.
Instrumentation: emit per-slot metrics: defined_class, residency_seconds, eviction_count, prefetch_hits, host_spill_count, and per-request tag to Console; add A/B toggle for rollout.
experiment_plan: Stage 0: Simulate adapter in offline trace replay using historical mixed-traffic traces (20% short-only, 40% mixed, 40% long-only). Verify memory residency and eviction model before touching runtime.
Stage 1: Canary on dedicated pool with 5% traffic and aggressive logging. Run for 48h and measure p50/p95/p99 latency, KV eviction delta, and GPU memory fragmentation index.
Stage 2: Expand to 25% across two regions with automated rollback at defined thresholds (p95 regression >8% or eviction increase >10%).
Stage 3: Gradual ramp to 100% with continuous monitoring and cost telemetry (tokens-per-GPU-second).
benchmarks_expected: Baseline p95 long-response trace: ~420ms. Target with adapter: <=360ms.
KV eviction rate baseline: 1.2 evictions/min per-GPU on mixed trace. Target: <=0.9 evictions/min.
Expected GPU memory fragmentation reduction: 6-12% depending on slab size and shard count.
Token throughput: small change (+/- 3%) expected during tuning; goal is no regression.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Predictor misclassification leading to over-reservation and wasted slab -> Mitigation: conservative default to buffered class and continuous learning with online calibrations.
Risk: Host spill adds CPU latency spikes on prefetch -> Mitigation: limit concurrent host prefetches, rate-limit spills per-GPU, and prioritize low-latency routes for pinning.
Risk: Increased complexity in scheduler may cause regression bugs -> Mitigation: isolate with feature flag, thorough unit/integration tests, and staged rollout with metric-based rollback.
Risk: Interaction with autoscaling (Dedicated) might change capacity signals -> Mitigation: expose occupancy signals to autoscaler and add safety floor for reserved capacity.
implementation_notes: Code changes live in runtime/batcher/seq_slot_adapter and runtime/kv/residency_manager modules. Expect ~650 LOC change and new metrics exporters.
Add two new Protobuf fields for request tag and slot_class; update SDK minor version to include optional tag header.
Gating: require updated unit tests for slot eviction heuristics and fuzz tests for turn_profile predictor.
Docs: Confluence doc at https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/runtime-sequenced-slot-adapter (draft) and a design PR linked below.
